quotes.text: Cross-border transactions are available in private preview.
Your account might be reviewed after activation to confirm eligibility.
Refunds for Afterpay payments are asynchronous and take up to 10 business days to complete. You can’t cancel Afterpay refunds.
Afterpay reviews your evidence and issues a final decision within 30 calendar days of dispute creation.
After the payment completes, expand `latest_charge` on the PaymentIntent to retrieve the Afterpay order ID from `latest_charge.payment_method_details.afterpay_clearpay.order_id`.

old_evidence.text: Afterpay and Clearpay only support domestic transactions

findings: The November page describes single-use Afterpay/Clearpay BNPL: Stripe redirects a customer for authentication and plan approval; Afterpay collects installments while the merchant is described as paid upfront, with standard payout schedule and instant provisional access as separate labels (new raw lines 5-15, 272-288). This does not prove funds settled in a bank account immediately, or that a redirect/return alone verifies a successful PaymentIntent.

Merchant and customer country lists remain AU, CA, GB, NZ and US with AUD/CAD/GBP/NZD/USD presentment (new raw lines 18-23, 95-114; old raw lines 18-24, 58-66). November qualifies domestic general availability with cross-border private preview, despite a broad geographic-coverage checkmark (new raw lines 111-119; old raw line 80). Current source line 19 and BNPL concept line 65 say domestic only without preview qualification, so correct both while not treating preview as general merchant eligibility.

Eligibility now includes B2C versus B2B, activation review/appeal, and a detailed prohibited/restricted MCC table. 'Restricted' permits possible use after additional account information, whereas 'prohibited' does not (new raw lines 18-40, 42-93). The old category list included bars/lounges but the new short list omits it; omission does not prove newly eligible, and the new MCC table/terms remain scoped to the captured page (old raw lines 128-141; new raw lines 25-93).

The five country Pay in 4 ranges remain AU 1-4000 AUD, CA 1-2000 CAD, NZ 1-4000 NZD, GB 1-1200 GBP; November shows US Pay in 4 at 1-2000 USD and monthly interest-bearing 6/12 months at 400-4000 USD (new raw lines 120-151; old raw lines 99-126). Existing source lines 21-36 and BNPL concept lines 65-67 already express the implied US tier overlap accurately. The standalone AU 1-4000 amount at new raw lines 115-117 must not be applied globally.

November adds 3-hour plan authorization, desktop website/mobile app-or-website routing and a PaymentIntent latest_charge.payment_method_details.afterpay_clearpay.order_id after completed payment (new raw lines 272-296). The BNPL concept line 75's '3-hour requires_action PaymentIntent expiry' is stronger than this overview's customer-authorization wording; this capture alone cannot establish the exact Intent status transition. Keep old integration-source route distinct.

November product matrix supports Checkout Sessions, PaymentIntents, full-page/embedded Checkout, Payment Links, Payment Element, in-app payments, Payment Method Messaging, Managed Payments and Connect. It excludes Billing, Invoicing, Customer Portal, Radar, Terminal, Express Checkout Element, SetupIntents, setup_future_usage and off-session payments (new raw lines 241-265). May page listed a private preview for one-time invoices (old raw lines 68-78), so retain that as dated prior preview and flag November Invoicing unsupported; no reason for the difference is established.

New capture details manual and partial capture but excludes multi-capture and over-capture; recurring, extended/flexible/incremental/decremental/re-authorization are unsupported (new raw lines 162-176). The prior page only stated manual capture yes and recurring no (old raw lines 34-56). Authorization, capture and payout remain distinct states.

Refunds must be submitted within 120 days; new page says asynchronous processing up to 10 business days, no cancellation and never reversal. It directs checking Refund.status and refund.updated/refund.failed, with failed amount returned to merchant Stripe balance and another customer refund method needed (new raw lines 178-202; old raw lines 175-177). A refund submission is not refund success, and the old current source line 40 covers only window/async.

The new dispute window is 120 days from purchase, one dispute per payment, full rather than partial disputes, 14 days for merchant evidence, and a final decision within 30 calendar days of dispute creation (new raw lines 184-187, 204-239). The prior wording anchored 30 days to evidence submission (old raw lines 149-173). Current source line 38 and BNPL concept line 69 leave the decision anchor unspecified; qualify the changed anchor and retain the old wording historically. Withheld disputed funds, final decision and fraud-liability coverage are distinct.

The May US Cash App Afterpay rebrand note and explicit Connect direct/destination/separate-charge types are absent from the November capture (old raw lines 8, 179-187; new raw lines 241-265, 266-270). Preserve them as dated historical statements in source lines 13, 17 and 44, not as November-verified integration/Connect details or as a proven reversal. Source line 17's blanket 'no integration changes required' drops May's 'unless you have custom Afterpay components' condition (old raw line 8). Source line 44's 'Correct MCCs required' also needs its old scope: connected accounts using Express Dashboard or a dashboard not hosted by Stripe (old raw lines 179-187). Source line 38's broad 'Afterpay covers fraud losses' should retain the captured limits of customer fraud or inability to repay installments and the possible request to stop/pause shipment (old raw line 151; new raw lines 237-239).
substantive_changes: Domestic GA now explicitly coexists with a cross-border private-preview pathway (old raw line 80; new raw lines 111-119); customer/merchant eligibility cannot be inferred from preview wording alone.

November adds activation review, prohibited/restricted MCC classification, detailed authorizations/capture support and product/API support; notably it marks Invoicing unsupported where May listed private-preview one-time invoices (old raw lines 68-78, 128-141; new raw lines 18-93, 162-187, 241-265).

Refund and dispute lifecycle details expand, including up-to-10-business-day asynchronous refunds, no refund cancellation, status/webhook outcomes, one full dispute, and 30-day decision measured from creation rather than May evidence submission (old raw lines 149-177; new raw lines 178-239).
November adds customer route and 3-hour authorization text, statement-descriptor handling, and a post-completion Afterpay order-ID path on latest_charge (new raw lines 272-296).

The former top-level property list and product list are reorganized into eligibility, capability and product matrices; the payment option country rows largely retain the same ranges and US tier overlap (old raw lines 16-78, 99-126; new raw lines 10-23, 111-151, 162-187, 241-265).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep May 6, 2026 Cash App Afterpay US rebrand note and no-integration-change qualifier as historical provenance; November omits the note but does not refute it (old raw line 8; new raw lines 5-15, 266-270).

Keep May one-time Invoicing private-preview claim dated and visibly paired with November's Invoicing unsupported matrix; do not imply preview was GA or determine why the status differs (old raw lines 68-78; new raw lines 251-265).

Keep older Connect charge-type list and MCC obligation as May-specific detail; November merely marks Connect supported and adds MCC eligibility classification, without repeating charge types (old raw lines 179-187; new raw lines 37-93, 241-265).

Keep country and amount schedules with their local currency and plan-specific limits, domestic GA/private-preview distinction, dynamic eligibility filtering with shipping-country before geocoded IP, and merchant responsibility when manually listing payment_method_types (old raw lines 80, 99-126, 189-196; new raw lines 103-160).

Keep May dispute decision anchored to evidence submission as dated May text, alongside November's creation-anchored wording and identical 14-day merchant evidence window; do not merge both into an unqualified 30-day guarantee (old raw lines 149-173; new raw lines 204-235).
conflicts: Current source line 19 and BNPL concept line 65 state absolute domestic-only, while November says domestic GA plus cross-border private preview (new raw lines 111-119; old raw line 80). Add reciprocal source/concept qualification, without presenting preview as broadly available.

May product support lists one-time Invoicing in private preview (old raw lines 68-78), while November matrix marks Invoicing unsupported (new raw lines 251-265). Keep dated two-way warning in the source and any concept claim about Invoicing; no retirement cause is demonstrated.

May dispute decision is within 30 calendar days of evidence submission (old raw line 173); November says within 30 calendar days of dispute creation (new raw lines 204-211). Current source line 38 and BNPL concept line 69 omit the anchor; make November anchor explicit and preserve May's dated different wording.

Current source line 42 and BNPL concept line 73 list bars as prohibited from May's short category list (old raw lines 128-141); November omits it from the short list but has a detailed MCC table and legal-terms pointer (new raw lines 25-93). Date the prior category claim and do not infer new permission from omission.

Source line 17 overgeneralizes May's no-integration-change rebrand note by omitting the custom-components exception; source line 44 generalizes a correct-MCC instruction beyond old raw's connected accounts using Express Dashboard or non-Stripe-hosted dashboard; source line 38 broadens fraud coverage beyond customer fraud or installment nonpayment (old raw lines 8, 151, 179-187; new raw lines 237-239).
unresolved_questions: The captured November page does not explain the one-time Invoicing private-preview to unsupported matrix change, or establish account-specific cross-border-preview enrollment (old raw lines 68-78; new raw lines 111-119, 251-265).

The overview's 3-hour customer authorization window does not itself specify PaymentIntent requires_action expiry or post-return status verification; the separate integration guide is only a related route in this job (new raw lines 272-288; BNPL concept line 75).
The top-level 'paid immediately' and 'instant provisional access' labels do not establish immediate bank settlement, which the same page labels standard payout schedule (new raw lines 7-15).

findings: Add November raw with date while preserving May rebrand and Connect charge-type provenance; update source line 19 to domestic GA plus cross-border private preview (old raw lines 8, 80, 179-187; new raw lines 111-119, 241-265).

Record November eligibility/MCC classification, capability/product support, 3-hour authorization, order-ID path, refund status/webhooks and dispute decision anchor (new raw lines 18-93, 162-202, 204-265, 272-296).
Pair May one-time Invoicing private preview with November unsupported matrix and do not treat either as account-specific live eligibility (old raw lines 68-78; new raw lines 251-265).

Repair older-summary scope: rebrand integration exception for custom Afterpay components, MCC instruction for specific connected-account dashboard types, and fraud coverage for customer fraud/repayment inability with potential shipment pause request (source lines 17, 38, 44; old raw lines 8, 151, 179-187; new raw lines 237-239).
conflicts: Source line 19's domestic-only statement omits November's cross-border private preview (new raw lines 111-119).
Source line 38's '30-day decision' lacks November's from-creation anchor and May's different from-evidence-submission anchor (old raw line 173; new raw line 211).

Source lines 17, 42, 44 retain May-only rebrand, bars and Connect details without explicit dated scope; November omission does not establish reversal (old raw lines 8, 128-141, 179-187; new raw lines 25-93, 241-270).

Source lines 17, 38, 44 additionally omit material old conditions on custom components, fraud/repayment-loss scope, and which connected dashboards need correctly set MCCs (old raw lines 8, 151, 179-187).
source_assessments.reason: The new capture adds consequential eligibility, lifecycle and support boundaries and exposes a material Invoicing contradiction; the mapped summary's unqualified domestic-only and historical details need careful dating.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/afterpay-clearpay, the November capture documents a single-use BNPL method in AU, CA, GB, NZ and US: Stripe redirects the customer to Afterpay for authentication and plan approval, the customer repays installments, and the merchant is described as paid upfront subject to a separate standard payout schedule (new raw lines 5-23, 95-118, 272-288). Domestic transactions are generally available; cross-border transactions are private preview. Dynamic country filtering checks shipping country before geocoded IP, while manual payment_method_types requires merchant-side eligibility handling (new raw lines 118, 153-160). Compared with May's domestic-only wording and one-time invoice preview, November marks Invoicing unsupported, adds MCC and capture constraints, refund/dispute states, and an order ID on latest_charge after completion (old raw lines 68-80, 128-177; new raw lines 18-93, 162-265, 290-296). source-stripe-afterpay-clearpay.md retains May country limits and tiers but needs preview and dated lifecycle differences; its rebrand, fraud and Connect summaries also omit old raw's custom-component, loss-scope and dashboard conditions (source lines 13-44; old raw lines 8, 151, 179-187).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/afterpay-clearpay, material November changes include the cross-border private-preview qualification, detailed prohibited/restricted MCCs, manual versus partial/multi capture support, full asynchronous refund outcomes, and a dispute decision deadline measured from dispute creation instead of May's evidence-submission wording (old raw lines 68-80, 128-177; new raw lines 18-93, 111-119, 162-239). November marks Invoicing unsupported even though May listed private-preview one-time invoices; source-stripe-afterpay-clearpay.md must preserve that historical claim with a reciprocal warning, as well as the May US rebrand and Connect charge-type details that November does not repeat (source lines 13-44; old raw lines 8, 68-78, 179-187; new raw lines 241-265). The country/plan amounts are largely stable, while matrix layout and route wording are presentational (old raw lines 99-126; new raw lines 120-151). Preview enrollment, customer approval, redirect return, PaymentIntent success, available merchant funds, capture, refund success and final dispute outcome are distinct conditions; neither provisional access nor a submitted refund settles those states.
